Study slides for the second course of IBM's *Understanding Quantum Information
and Computation* series, taught by John Watrous. The course asks where quantum
computers beat classical ones, and proves it for four families of problems.

**Prerequisite:** the course *Basics of quantum information* (qubits, quantum
circuits, measurement). [Original course
page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/fundamentals-of-quantum-algorithms).

## Lectures

::: {.lesson-table}
| | Lecture | What it covers | Original |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Quantum query algorithms](lectures/01-quantum-query-algorithms.qmd) | The query model; Deutsch, Deutsch–Jozsa, Bernstein–Vazirani and Simon's algorithms; phase kickback | [video](https://youtu.be/2wticzHE1vs) · [slides](https://ibm.box.com/public/static/keh3p0vnrptftpk6o5kabvjewj8psube.pdf) |
| 2 | [Quantum algorithmic foundations](lectures/02-quantum-algorithmic-foundations.qmd) | Factoring and GCD; circuit size, depth and asymptotic cost; running classical computations reversibly on a quantum computer | [video](https://youtu.be/2wxxvwRGANQ) · [slides](https://ibm.box.com/public/static/yic6g33o4xn103oaay8xqbbwyc64d0jz.pdf) |
| 3 | [Phase estimation and factoring](lectures/03-phase-estimation-and-factoring.qmd) | Spectral theorem; phase estimation; the quantum Fourier transform; order finding and Shor's algorithm | [video](https://youtu.be/4nT0BTUxhJY) · [slides](https://ibm.box.com/public/static/jxase3mly99ui1n1fg8pvp6bzymbdgrh.pdf) |
| 4 | [Grover's algorithm](lectures/04-grover-algorithm.qmd) | Unstructured search; the Grover operation as a rotation; choosing the number of iterations | [video](https://youtu.be/hnpjC8WQVrQ) · [slides](https://ibm.box.com/public/static/03clwlnuz7ygbrctbrm7xofngf5f0urs.pdf) |
:::

## How to study with these slides

1. Watch the lesson video, or read the original lesson.
2. Go through the deck. Press **S** for speaker notes: they hold the steps of
   the proofs that do not fit on a slide.
3. Close the deck and redo each derivation on paper. The decks end with a
   recap slide; it should read as obvious by then.

The badge exam is linked from the [original course
page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/fundamentals-of-quantum-algorithms).
